title: Document
description: The front matter of a prose document: a README, a guide, a note under docs/ — anything the layer carries that is not an object of a stricter kind. Front matter is optional on this kind, and a document with none is a document, not a broken one; this describes what must hold when there is some. The contract is deliberately small, because a document that needed more fields than these is something else and should declare its own kind. A document that says `kind: context` is a context document and is held to context.schema.json instead.

title.description: The document's title. Absent means the first level-one Markdown heading is the title, which is how most documents carry one.

description.description: One line saying what this document is for. It is what a listing shows, so it says the subject rather than restating the title.

kind.description: The kind this document declares itself to be, when it is not a plain document. Only a kind the distribution lists as declarable is accepted; anything else is a mismatch rather than a new kind.

status.description: Whether this document still applies. Absent means active: a document with no status is in force, because the alternative is a layer where nothing is quite binding.

superseded_by.description: The repository-relative path of the document that replaces this one. Required reading whenever status is superseded, which is why the two are coupled below.

updated.description: The day the content last changed, YYYY-MM-DD. Not a modification time — a person sets it when what the document says changes, and leaves it alone for a typo.

tags.description: Free tags for retrieval. They carry no behaviour: nothing dispatches on a tag, so a tag can be added without changing what anything does.

then.description: A document declared superseded names what supersedes it. A dead end that says only 'do not read this' leaves the reader with nowhere to go.
